title: Moreno Valley Home Energy Rebates 2026: MVU and SCE Programs | HomePowerRebate
desc: Moreno Valley home energy programs in 2026: Moreno Valley Utility's tune-up rebate and bill discounts, SCE's offers for the rest of the city, and what is full.
lead: Moreno Valley has its own city electric utility, Moreno Valley Utility (MVU), that serves part of the city, and Southern California Edison (SCE) serves the rest. Which one bills you decides your programs. MVU publishes few dollar amounts online. We read its pages and forms on October 2, 2026.
cards_heading: What is open in Moreno Valley
cards_intro: MVU customers use MVU's programs, and SCE customers use SCE's. MVU's page says its rebates are limited, not guaranteed, and may end without notice.

cards.title: MVU AC or heat pump tune-up
cards.note: Up to 2 units per location, for existing systems at least a year old, with a NATE-certified technician.

cards.title: MVU rate discount
cards.note: A discount on electric energy charges for qualified families, based on household income. Needs an application and an IRS transcript.

cards.title: MVU audit and direct install
cards.note: A full home energy audit and a fixed set of upgrades for very high energy users and low-income participants: AC tune-ups, duct testing and sealing, filter changes and efficient lighting.

cards.title: EV charger panel upgrade (SCE Charge Ready Home)
cards.note: Income-qualified customers only, below 80% of area median income or on an assistance program. A Level 2 charger must be installed within 180 days.

after_cards:
Check your bill first

MVU serves part of Moreno Valley and SCE serves the rest. The utility named on your electric bill decides which list applies. MVU customers can reach MVU at 951-413-3500 or mvuprograms@moval.org. SCE customers should see the SCE programs on our San Bernardino page.
sections:
MVU's residential program offers include energy audits and direct install, an ENERGY STAR appliance rebate, central AC and heat pump replacement, central AC and heat pump tune-up, Cooling Rewards, a custom energy efficiency program, a shade tree incentive and a solar generator rebate for medical baseline customers. MVU's incentives flyer says its rebates cover ENERGY STAR refrigerators, freezers, washers, dishwashers, ceiling fans and room air conditioners, plus LED lights, attic insulation, Low-E windows and doors, solar attic fans, variable speed pool pumps, solar water heaters and electric heat pump water heaters, and that many pay extra when bought locally in Moreno Valley.

We could not find dollar amounts for the heat pump replacement or the other items on MVU's public pages or its flyer, so we do not quote them. Call MVU before you buy. The only amount we could confirm is the $75 tune-up.
The bill discount may beat any rebate

MVU's rate reduction program gives qualified families a 23% or 35% discount on electric energy charges, depending on income. Applying requires a completed application and an original IRS Transcript of Return. For a household that uses a lot of electricity, a standing discount on every bill can be worth more than a one-time rebate, so check eligibility first.
Direct install is a free option

MVU's Residential Energy Audit and Direct Install program targets very high energy use customers and participants in its low-income program. Eligible households receive a full in-home audit with specific recommendations and a fixed set of maintenance and upgrades at no cost, such as tune-ups and duct testing and sealing. If your electric bills are high, ask whether you qualify before you pay for any of that work yourself.

SCE customers can use its smart thermostat credit ($75), Charge Smart (up to $100), Charge Ready Home for income-qualified EV panel work (up to $4,200) and Energy Savings Assistance. We found no SCE rebate for a heat pump or battery (SCE's Marketplace page). The federal 25C and 25D tax credits ended after December 31, 2025. TECH Clean California and federal HEEHRA are fully reserved for single-family homes and take requests on hold only.

Moreno Valley's average January low over 2015 to 2024 was 5.9°C (about 43°F), the coolest in the Inland Empire cities we cover, with a coldest recorded day of -3.7°C, and about 5.5 peak sun hours a day. A standard heat pump handles that, though cold winter nights make it worth asking your installer about low-temperature output and defrost. Summers are hot, so cooling sets the size. See Riverside for how a neighboring city's utility pays for a heat pump.
installers_intro: These Moreno Valley heat pump and HVAC companies have the best Google ratings, listed by rating and then review count. We are not paid to list anyone. For MVU's tune-up rebate, the technician must be NATE certified, so ask.
claim_steps: Look at your electric bill and confirm whether MVU or SCE supplies your power.
If you are an MVU customer, ask MVU about the rate discount and the audit and direct install program.
For an AC or heat pump tune-up, use a NATE-certified technician and send MVU the signed application and test data.
Call MVU at 951-413-3500 before buying any equipment, to confirm what the current rebate is.
If you are an SCE customer, ask SCE about Energy Savings Assistance and enroll a thermostat for the $75 credit.
faq: Who supplies electricity in Moreno Valley?
Moreno Valley Utility serves part of the city and Southern California Edison serves the rest. Check your bill.
How much is MVU's tune-up rebate?
$75 per air conditioner or heat pump unit, up to 2 units per location, for existing systems at least a year old, with a NATE-certified technician.
A 23% or 35% discount on electric energy charges for qualified families, depending on income.
Is there a heat pump replacement rebate?
MVU lists a central AC and heat pump replacement program but we could not find the amount online, so call MVU. We found no SCE heat pump rebate.
Does MVU pay extra for buying locally?
MVU's flyer says many incentives have an additional rebate amount if purchased locally within the City of Moreno Valley.
